issues.detail: The Greek 'προσαγαγη' (pro-sēgēgē) means 'to lead/bring near' or 'to present'. The Vietnamese 'dẫn chúng ta đến cùng Đức Chúa Trời' (lead us to the very [presence of] God) is a slightly different nuance than 'presenting us before God', but more importantly, the Greek 'προσαγαγη' is an infinitive of purpose. The Vietnamese 'để dẫn' captures this, but 'đến cùng' adds a superlative sense ('to the very...') not present in the Greek.

The Greek 'προσαγαγη' is an infinitive of purpose (ἵνα... προσαγαγῇ), but the Vietnamese 'để dẫn chúng ta đến cùng Đức Chúa Trời' implies a destination/result. However, the more critical issue is the phrasing of 'προσαγαγη'. In many contexts, this refers to presenting us *before* God. The Vietnamese 'đến cùng' (to the very/ultimate) is an addition of intensity.
